identity.title: Integrative analysis of pooled CRISPR screens provide functional insights into AD GWAS risk genes.

content.abstract: Microglia pathways such as lipid transport and metabolism, phagocytosis, and lysosomal function are implicated Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology, but the mechanisms underlying these pathways remain poorly understood. To map these pathways, custom CRISPR activation and interference (CRISPRa/i) libraries were constructed targeting 203 microglial and genome-wide association study (GWAS)-associated risk genes. Pooled CRISPRa/i screens in THP-1 cells identified core functional regulators of lipid metabolism and lysosomal function, a subset of which were validated in primary macrophages. We also captured transcriptomic changes caused by these genes by performing Perturb-seq in primary macrophages. Through non-negative matrix factorization, we identified five gene programs altered by our perturbation library. We then used an integrative analysis of functional screen data with Perturb-seq data that enabled us to uncover novel functions and genetic relationships between perturbations. This multidimensional resource links genetic perturbations to phenotypes and transcriptional programs, establishing a scalable framework for systematic gene discovery in neurodegeneration and beyond.
